correctness.rationale: Meet preservation follows from order preservation on a total chain. Every nucleus is ceiling to an arbitrary fixed-point subset containing top; hence exactly 2^(n-1) nuclei. Two properly crossing fibers force different composites on a boundary input; nested/disjoint fiber partitions imply equal composites by comparing the blocks containing x and the endpoint. All pairwise compatible intervals form a laminar hierarchy; maximality forces every compatible interval-collapse map, all leaves and root; no internal node may have >=3 children (adjoin two consecutive children), so maximal hierarchies are exactly ordered full binary trees. Frontier cuts are exactly compatible fiber partitions and maximal families. Counting cuts gives q recursion. In ordered-pair scanning, between consecutive boundaries shared by both maps, only one exclusive boundary type may occur; two-state transfer matrix [[2,1],[2,2]] gives characteristic t^2-4t+2 and b recurrence. Fresh independently written mapping enumeration tested commutation against laminar fibers for all pairs at n=1..6 and reproduced counts 1,4,14,48,164,560. Finite tests corroborate; the hierarchy and matrix arguments prove all n.

originality.rationale: The classical Catalan monoid contains non-idempotent order-preserving extensive maps and its established structure does not by itself classify maximal commuting families of its idempotents, which correspond to Heyting nuclei on the chain. The asserted correspondence to full ordered binary trees, sizes of individual maximal families and rational ordered-pair recurrence are compared at the statement/implication level. No published directly equivalent complete classification was found in checked material; some semigroup literature may have a hidden formulation.
residual_risks: A theorem about maximal commuting idempotents in Catalan or related Kiselman monoids could encode the same tree classification under semigroup terminology.
Independent brute-force checks stop at n=6; infinite result rests on analytic proof.
Other lattices and non-idempotent Catalan monoid elements are outside scope.
